model_annotations.English: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between Block Index and Sensitivity for 4-Fbit and 2-Fbit data. The horizontal axis, labeled “Block Index”, displays categories numbered sequentially from 0 to 27, with each number representing a discrete block index. The vertical axis, labeled “Sensitivity”, utilizes a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³, with tick labels displayed at intervals of 10⁻⁴ and 10⁻⁵.  There are 28 bars for each data series, arranged side-by-side and sorted by Block Index. The 4-Fbit data is represented by blue bars, varying in length from approximately 3.5 x 10⁻⁵ at Block Index 6, to 1.0 x 10⁻³ at Block Index 27. The 2-Fbit data is represented by green bars, ranging in length from approximately 2.5 x 10⁻⁵ at Block Index 6, to 3.0 x 10⁻⁵ at Block Index 27; these bars are consistently shorter than the corresponding 4-Fbit bars. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlines, or annotations.
model_annotations.German: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between “Block Index” and “Sensitivity” for two data series, “4-Fbit” and “2-Fbit”. The horizontal axis is labeled “Block Index” and contains numerical categories ranging from 0 to 27, listed in ascending order. The vertical axis is labeled “Sensitivity” and uses a logarithmic scale, with tick marks at 10⁻⁵, 10⁻⁴, and 10⁻³, representing the scale’s range. Each Block Index has two bars: a blue bar representing “4-Fbit” and a green bar representing “2-Fbit”. For Block Index 0, the “4-Fbit” bar reaches approximately 2.5 x 10⁻³, while the “2-Fbit” bar reaches approximately 3.5 x 10⁻⁴.  At Block Index 27, the “4-Fbit” bar reaches approximately 9 x 10⁻³, and the “2-Fbit” bar reaches approximately 5 x 10⁻⁴.  Generally, the “4-Fbit” bars are taller than corresponding “2-Fbit” bars, and the height of the “4-Fbit” bars tends to increase as Block Index increases from 0 to 27; the “2-Fbit” bars exhibit a more moderate and less consistently increasing trend. No bars appear to be visually emphasized.
